nodes.title: Lattices and bilattices
nodes.statement: For a complete discrete valuation ring R with fraction field K, uniformizer t and residue field k, a lattice in a finite-dimensional K-space V is a finite free R-submodule spanning V. A bilattice is (V,L1,L2); morphisms are K-linear maps preserving both lattices. Define decreasing trace filtration trFil^i(L1/tL1)=image((t^i L2)∩L1→L1/tL1). The elementary-divisor type is the multiset of a_j with L2=⊕R t^{a_j}e_j for a basis of L1.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Use elementary divisors over the complete DVR.
Define the intersection before taking its image; quotienting L2 alone gives the wrong trace filtration.
acceptance: Checks distinguish the filtration from the lattice and are invariant under a change of uniformizer.

nodes.title: Recovery from a filtration
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete characteristic-zero discrete valuation ring, with fraction field K, algebraically closed residue field C and uniformizer t, with its coefficient field embedded compatibly in R. For a connected linear group G and a cocharacter mu over an algebraically closed coefficient field, the pointwise BB map on the good type-[mu] cell is bijective if all Ad(mu)-weights are ≤1. For the second assertion, let a group Gamma act on R preserving its maximal ideal; assume C^Gamma lies in the coefficient field, G and [mu] are defined over C^Gamma, and Gamma preserves the line (C^Gamma)·t and acts on it by an infinite-order character. Then the Gamma-fixed part of this good cell is exactly the canonical lifts of the C^Gamma-rational flags. In particular this applies to B_dR and the Galois action of a discretely valued p-adic K0⊂C with infinite cyclotomic extension. The fixed-point assertion concerns the good cell, not arbitrary lattices.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: For the weight-bound statement compute positive-loop root coordinates and their truncation degrees.
For Galois invariance apply the cyclotomic action on graded B_dR and eliminate negative non-invariant coefficients.
acceptance: An adjoint weight ≥2 leaves a nontrivial BB fibre; the assertion is not made for all lattices without the Galois hypothesis.

nodes.title: Specialization dominance
nodes.statement: Write G=M⋉U over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. For a bilattice with Levi type [mu_M], let [mu] be its induced G-cocharacter class. In every representation rho, rho([mu]) is dominated by the actual vector-bilattice type, with equal determinant degree. Equality in one closed faithful representation is equivalent to goodness of type [mu]. This is a comparison of types, not semicontinuity of all non-reductive cells in families.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Conjugate the Levi lattice to standard form.
Order unipotent weight factors and use exterior-power lattice bounds for dominance.
Equality in a faithful representation forces the residual weight factors to be integral in the required coordinates.
acceptance: In the G_a extension, the Levi type is (0,0) while the actual GL_2 type is (1,−1); this fixes the dominance orientation.

nodes.title: G-isocrystals and basic classes
nodes.statement: For connected linear G/Q_p, a G-isocrystal is an exact tensor functor Rep_Qp G→Isoc(Q_p-breve). Its isomorphism classes form B(G), equivalently sigma-conjugacy classes in G(Q_p-breve). Define its Newton homomorphism nu:D→G over Q_p-breve and call it basic when nu is central in G. Define B(G,[mu]) by the inverse image of B(M,[mu_M]) for the reductive Levi quotient M=G/R_uG.

Identify the representation functor of b with Frobenius rho(b) sigma.
Obtain Newton grading representationwise from Dieudonné–Manin.

nodes.title: Sigma-centralizer and inner form

nodes.title: Pointwise p-adic Hodge structures

nodes.title: Pointwise admissible pairs
nodes.statement: An admissible pair over C is a finite-dimensional isocrystal W/Q_p-breve together with a B_dR+-lattice L_et⊂W⊗B_dR such that the modified bundle E(W)_{L_et} is semistable of slope zero. Define V_et=H^0(E(W)_{L_et}), the comparison c_dR:V_et⊗B_dR≅W⊗B_dR, and L_dR=c_dR^-1(W⊗B_dR+).

Slope-zero classification trivializes the modification and yields the comparison via evaluation.

nodes.title: Good reduction and analytic lattices
nodes.statement: Let C0=W(k_C)[1/p] inside C and let C0bar denote its algebraic closure inside C. nodes.title: Two-lattice CM criterion
nodes.statement: Write C0=W(k_C)[1/p] and let C0bar be its algebraic closure inside C. For a basic admissible pair over C, having both its étale lattice (relative to W) and its de Rham lattice (relative to V_et) defined by filtrations over finite extensions of C0 is equivalent to having CM. In the CM case the étale lattice can be defined over Q_p-breve-bar and the de Rham lattice over Q_p-bar. Equivalently a good-reduction p-adic Hodge structure has C0bar-analytic de Rham lattice exactly when it has CM. For a C0bar-analytic admissible pair without basicness, if its de Rham lattice is also C0bar-analytic, the slope filtration lifts to subpairs and its graded subpairs have CM; the original extension need not split or have CM.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Reduce the CM direction to a torus; its flag varieties are points, so the character/cocharacter lattice description makes both filtrations algebraic over the stated smaller fields.
For the converse the algebraic filtration has an open MG orbit fixed by its field of definition, forcing central cocharacters and then a torus.
In the nonbasic case use the lifted slope filtration and apply the basic statement to each graded part.
acceptance: The nonbasic refinement yields CM graded pieces, not a semisimplicity or splitting assertion.

nodes.title: The trivial-filtration lattice functor
nodes.statement: For smooth rigid X over a p-adic field L, define M0(E,∇) as Scholze’s B_dR+-local system attached to the flat bundle with trivial filtration. Descend and compare tensor products and strict morphisms.

nodes.title: Smooth rigid lattice–filtration comparison
nodes.statement: For smooth rigid X over a p-adic field L, the functor (E,∇,F)↦(M0(E),M(E,F)) is fully faithful on Griffiths-transversal filtered flat bundles. Recover the trace flag on a pro-étale chart.

Compare its canonical lattice with the original and use uniqueness in the induction.

nodes.title: Non-reductive de Rham Grassmannians

nodes.title: Grassmannian geometry and Schubert loci
nodes.statement: For connected linear G, Gr_G is separated, partially proper and an increasing union of closed locally spatial diamonds. nodes.statement: Fix a Levi G=M⋉U and a closed faithful rho:G→GL(V). In Gr_G×_{Gr_M}Gr_[mu_M], the cell Gr_[mu] is exactly the inverse image under rho of the closed Schubert bound Gr_GL(V),≤rho(mu). nodes.title: Rigid sources and Griffiths transversality
nodes.statement: For a seminormal rigid S/L and a map S^diamond→Gr_G whose Levi projection lands in Gr_[mu_M], the map factors through Gr_[mu]. BB identifies such maps with filtrations of type [mu^-1] on the trivial G-bundle whose restriction to the smooth locus is Griffiths transversal for the trivial connection. Descend the flag and its canonical lattice along the resolution and its fibre product by seminormal full faithfulness.

nodes.title: Adjoint-weight BB criterion
nodes.statement: BB:Gr_[mu]→Fl_[mu^-1]^diamond is an isomorphism iff all weights of Ad∘mu on Lie G are ≤1. If any weight exceeds 1, BB has no section over any nonempty open subdiamond of the flag variety. For reductive G this condition is equivalent to minuscule [mu]; for non-reductive G it is a one-sided bound. In particular every rigid analytic map into Gr_Ga is zero, although Gr_Ga has many geometric points.

For the bounded case identify the quotient with the flag.
For the converse a hypothetical section yields a filtration with impossible Griffiths-transverse differential in a weight >1 direction.

nodes.title: G-families and canonical reduction
nodes.statement: A neutral G-admissible pair is an exact tensor functor A:Rep_Qp G→AdmPair^neutral(Y) such that, at every geometric y, omega_y∘A is isomorphic to the standard fibre functor. These isomorphisms are required to exist, not chosen as part of the object. With a chosen geometric fibre trivialization define H=MG(A,y)≤G from its generated tensor subcategory. H is connected. If Y is connected, its canonical H-reduction is again neutral, and its isocrystal functor is isomorphic to W_bH for some b_H∈H(Q_p-breve). With g sending f(b_H) to b by sigma-conjugation, the classifying map factors through the H-admissible locus. For disconnected Y this assertion is made componentwise, not with one universal neutral reduction.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: A finite-monodromy tensor quotient is pointwise trivial by HK I 5.1.6.
Its fixed isocrystal maps and lattices therefore make it globally trivial, proving connectedness.
On connected Y the fibre-form torsor class is locally constant and fixed by its value at y, so the canonical reduction is neutral.
Apply isocrystal classification and the tensor-Isom trivialization.

nodes.statement: Let S be a geometrically connected seminormal rigid analytic variety over a p-adic L⊇Q_p-breve, and let A be a neutral G-admissible pair on S^diamond. Then its bilatticed G-local system is good and has a single type [mu], with [mu] defined over L. nodes.title: Neutral Hodge structures in families

Morphisms are fixed graded Q_p-linear maps preserving L_dR. A G-structure is an exact tensor functor into this category; its MT group at y is defined from the generated tensor subcategory. nodes.title: The Hodge period domain
nodes.statement: Fix a connected linear G and [mu] for which B(G,[mu^-1]) has a G-basic class. Let X_[mu]⊂Gr_[mu^-1] be the open locus where the modified trivial bundle is basic. nodes.title: Special Hodge subvarieties
nodes.statement: For connected H≤G and type [mu_H] inducing [mu_G], with a basic class for H whose image in B(G) is the ambient G-basic class, the map X_[mu_H]→X_[mu_G] is the subgroup period map. nodes.title: Borel and parabolic boundary examples
nodes.statement: Let H be the upper triangular Borel of G=GL_2, and let mu_G(t)=diag(t^-1,1). Write L_[a:c]=R^2+R xi^-1(a e1+c e2). For b=diag(p,1), G-admissibility means a≠0, whereas H-admissibility in the full preimage means c=0. Thus a c≠0 gives an ambient-admissible point that is not subgroup-admissible. With b=diag(1,p), the particular H-cell <e1,xi^-1(e2+x e1)> is A^1 and maps isomorphically to the G-admissible part P^1 minus [e1]; both loci are H-admissible there. Separately, for G=GL_3 and H stabilizing the span of e1,e2, the family <e1,e2+(z/xi)e1,e3+(1/xi)e1> has constant G-type (1,0,−1); its GL_2×GL_1 Levi type is (1,−1;0) for z≠0 and (0,0;0) at z=0. Therefore a subgroup cell can fail to be closed in an ambient fixed-type cell, and subgroup Schubert decompositions need not be intersections with ambient cells.

proofSteps: Compute elementary divisors and induced Levi lattices in the displayed bases.
Separate G-triviality of the modified bundle from the H-fibre-functor neutrality condition.
Compare the nonzero-z locus with its limit at zero.
acceptance: The Borel’s b is diag(1,p) for the A^1 assertion; the reversed diagonal describes a different example.

nodes.title: Comparison of the three special notions
nodes.statement: Assume b is basic. A closed connected subdiamond of M_C is special iff it is both Hodge special and Hodge–Tate special. nodes.title: Hodge-exceptional and generic loci

nodes.title: Generic-point period submersion
nodes.statement: After replacing a connected rigid family by its canonical full motivic group, let a connected closed rigid target Y at an opposite analytic level contain the image of its lifted family. A Hodge-generic classical point yields an orbit K0·y⊂Y(C) for some compact open K0≤G(Q_p). After translating the lift and shrinking K0, choose a smooth locally closed stratum V⊂Y containing this orbit on which the flag-map differential has constant rank. That rank equals dim Fl_[mu]. Griffiths transversality then forces all Ad(mu)-weights ≥−1; BB for the inverse type is an isomorphism, and Y is the connected component of that finite-level ambient space containing y.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Pass to the strict completed maximal unramified extension of the residue field of the generic classical point and use an open inertia orbit contained in the original orbit.
Descend through strata of strictly decreasing dimension until rank is constant on a stratum meeting that orbit openly.
Constant rank produces a transverse vanishing coordinate if rank is deficient.
Pull it back along the submersive G(C)-orbit map; its vanishing on K0 contradicts the identity theorem across Q_p.
Surjectivity and Griffiths transversality give the adjoint bound, then the full-dimensional closed-subspace criterion gives the component equality.
acceptance: This proves submersion at the translated lift in the selected smooth stratum; it does not claim smoothness at every original point.

nodes.title: Bi-analytic Ax–Lindemann theorem
nodes.statement: Let G/Q_p be connected linear, [mu] a cocharacter class admitting a G-basic [b]∈B(G,[mu^-1]), choose b and let M=M_{b,[mu]}. Let L/Q_p-breve([mu]) be p-adic and C=completed algebraic closure of L. Hodge (respectively Hodge–Tate) special subvarieties are closed irreducible analytic sets in their respective structures. The Hodge–Tate analytic closure of an irreducible Hodge analytic set is a Hodge–Tate-special subvariety whenever its defining family of containing closed rigid analytic subdiamonds is nonempty; if that family is empty the closure is all M_C. Interchanging Hodge and Hodge–Tate gives the second assertion. Consequently the closed bi-analytic subdiamonds, with the irreducibility convention in analytic_closures, are exactly the special subvarieties.

proofSteps: Reduce the lifted analytic set to its connected canonical motivic group H and its fixed type.
In the nonempty-index case apply the submersion argument to every containing connected rigid level target.
Each target contains the same component of M^H, whose lower adjoint bound now makes it Hodge–Tate special.
Its special analytic closedness identifies the intersection with that component.
Use basic duality for the reversed statement and both bounds for the bi-analytic consequence.
acceptance: The empty-index clause and the basicness hypothesis are part of the theorem.

nodes.title: Minuscule Ax–Lindemann theorem
nodes.statement: For connected linear G/Q_p and [mu] whose adjoint weights all lie in [−1,1], basic [b]∈B(G,[mu^-1]), L as above and C its completed algebraic closure, the opposite analytic closure of any irreducible Hodge or Hodge–Tate analytic set is special. The two analytic closures are the inverse-limit Zariski closures in the corresponding rigid towers. For an algebraic Z′⊂Fl_[mu] over its reflex field, an irreducible component Z of Z′_C∩X_[mu], and a connected component Ztilde of pi_HT^-1(Z), its image’s rigid Zariski closure in a Hodge finite level is a finite-level special subvariety. The zero-dimensional case agrees with the two-lattice CM criterion.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Use BB isomorphisms on both sides of minuscule data.
Finite-level spaces are rigid, so the empty-index exception is absent.
Identify the two topology-based closures with AP11’s intersections and apply the theorem.

nodes.title: Variations of p-adic Hodge structure
nodes.statement: For smooth rigid S/L, a variation of p-adic Hodge structure is a finite Q-graded de Rham Q_p-local system L=⊕L_lambda for which each fibre (L_lambda,M0,lambda) is a weight-lambda p-adic Hodge structure. Here M0 is the lattice from the trivial filtration on the associated flat bundle, while the original local system determines the étale rational structure. A G-variation is an exact tensor functor Rep_Qp G into this category. A pro-étale K-torsor for open K≤G(Q_p) is de Rham if its associated representation local systems are de Rham, equivalently for one closed faithful representation.

Form M0 after forgetting the Hodge filtration of the flat bundle.
Impose the pure bundle condition on each graded fibre.
acceptance: The Q_p-local system is allowed to have monodromy here; this is a distinct family notion from the neutral category.

nodes.title: Katz–Igusa obstruction
nodes.statement: On the ordinary locus of a connected finite-level modular curve without p-level, the Katz–Igusa Z_p×-tower trivializing the unit-root isocrystal equals the crystalline-frame cover for the associated rank-one de Rham torsor. Its surjective infinite Z_p× monodromy prevents refinement by a rigid analytic de Jong cover of the asserted kind; its inverse-limit adic realization is not a finite-type rigid analytic variety.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.

Use connectedness of the Igusa tower to obtain its full monodromy.

acceptance: This example is a boundary to rigid refinement, not a disproof of the potentially unramified expectation.

nodes.title: Products of Shimura curves
nodes.statement: Let D/Q be a quaternion algebra split at infinity and ramified at p, with neat level away from p and maximal local level; let B be the inner form definite at infinity and split at p. For a product of n associated curves over Q_p-breve, each chosen component has a Čerednik–Drinfeld presentation Omega^n/Gamma, with Gamma the product of the arithmetic component stabilizers. At infinite level the local product M of Drinfeld spaces and the global perfectoid tower have compatible Hodge–Tate maps and differ by the corresponding arithmetic quotient. Locally in the analytic topology this is the local period diagram. Thus the opposite analytic closure of a lifted irreducible analytic set is the transported image of the appropriate local special subvariety.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Apply the supplied Čerednik–Drinfeld theorem separately to each factor, tracking determinant components and their stabilizers.
Form the product diagram and the compatible perfectoid inverse levels.
Proper discontinuity makes the finite-level uniformization analytic-locally an isomorphism.
Transport AP11 through that diagram; the bi-algebraic Chambert-Loir–Loeser theorem concerns a different pair of algebraic structures and is comparison context, not an input to this implication.
acceptance: The quaternion algebras D and B have opposite local behaviour at p and infinity; retain the arithmetic quotient at every level.
